intended_object: The canonical isomorphism Spec_X(p_* 𝒪_V) ≅ V for an affine morphism p : V → X. It recovers an affine X-scheme from the quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-algebra of its functions (Stacks 01LL), and it is the component of the counit of the equivalence between affine X-schemes and quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-algebras. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition applies `asIso` to `relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme`. That map is built by gluing, over the affine opens U of X, the standard charts Spec Γ(V, p⁻¹U) → p⁻¹U ⊆ V. To get these charts it identifies the sections of p_*𝒪_V over U with Γ(V, p⁻¹U).

The instance `isIso_relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme` is proved by checking the map locally on the cover p⁻¹U. Separate lemmas show the map commutes with the maps to X (`relativeSpecFunctionsToScheme_comp`) and is natural in morphisms over X. This is exactly the standard canonical isomorphism.

The generality is the natural one: any base scheme X (no affineness needed) and any affine morphism p. The hypothesis `IsAffineHom` is needed for the statement to make sense.

Mathlib at this commit has no relative Spec construction (grepping for "relativeSpec" in Mathlib finds nothing), so there is no Mathlib counterpart.

The isomorphism is stated as one of schemes rather than of X-schemes, but the compatibility with X is proved separately and used to build `relativeSpecCounit`, so nothing is missing.
